  FISCAL IMPACT:  There is no impact to the General Fund, The proposed Agreement is for an
  amount not to exceed $68,603, and it will be funded with Water Funds budgeted in the Fiscal
  Year 2025/26 Public Works Operating Budget,

  ANALYSJS:  Construction of the project is anticipated to require 120 working days to complete
  and will involve more than 150 hours of construction management and inspection services. Due
  to current staffing limitations, the Public Works Department's Engineering Division does not
  have sufficierit in-house resources to perform these services while maintaining ongoing
  operational  and capital  improvement  responsibilities,

  To support project delivery, staff issued a Request for Task Proposals ("RFTP") to the City's
  four prequalified As-Needed Engineering firms and received two proposals, Following review of
  the submitted proposals and qrialifications, staff determined that NS75 is the most qualified firm
  to provide the requiredconstnuctionmanagement and inspection services for the pro5ect.

  BACKGROUND:  The City's water system consists of more than 135 miles of water
  pipelines, eight active groundwater wells, and multiple water production facilities. One of the
  City's primary water production sites is located at South Gate Park and includes four
  groundwater wells, a water reservoir, and * on-site treatment system, Currently, groundwater
  1

  322
 produced  by two  of the wells  has been impacted  by PFAS  contamination.  If additional  wells  at
the site are impacted  and required  to be taken  offline,  it is critical  that  the reservoir  remain
operational  to maintain  reliable  water  service,  adequate  system  pressure,  and fire protection  for
the community.

To address  this need,  staff  is proposing  the South  Gate Park Reservoir  Interconnection  Project,
which  is budgeted  in the Fiscal  Year  2025/26  Capital  Improvement  Program.  The project  will
construct  a water  mainline  connection  between  the reservoir  and the City's  water  distribution
system,  allowing  the City  to directly  supply  potable  water  to the reservoir  independent  of certain
well  operations.  The  project  will  also improve  operational  reliability  by allowing  the City  to
continue  delivering  water  from  the  South  Gate  Park  reservoir  when  groundwater  wells  are
temporarily  unavailable  due to maintenance,  equipment  failure,  or regulatory  requirements.

On April  20,  2026,  an RFTP  was  issued  to the  four  (4)  prequalified  as-needed  engineering
consulting  firms,  and two (2) proposals  were received  as summarized  below.

  Consultant  Fee Proposal
  NV5  $68,603
  Interwest  $97,895

A  selection  cornrnittee  consisting  of the  City's  Associate  Engineer  and  Water  Resources  &
Development  Division  Manager,  evaluated  the proposals.  All  consultants  met the qualifications
criteria  which  included  construction  manager,  inspector  experience,  and  labor  compliance.
However,  NV5  received  the highest  ranking  as the proposed  construction  manager  and inspector
provided  the  same  services  in  a previously  successful  phase  and  is recommended  for  the
contract.  NV5  provides  the following  benefits  to the project:

  *  Competitive  Fees - The fee proposal  is $68,603  and is competitive,  as it represents  the
  lowest  proposal  received  from  the RFTP.

  *  Experienced  Construction  Manager  - The Construction  Manager  has over 30 years of
  experience.

  @  Qualified  Staff  -  NV5  offers  a qualified  team  with  experience,  knowledge,  and
  professionalism  for the Project.  NV5  has licensed  engineers,  construction  and program
  managers,  inspectors,  office  engineers,  technicians,  and adtninistrative  support  to manage
  the Project.

  *  Qualified  Team  - NV5's  in-house  team  will  provide  special  inspections,  if necessary,
  testing  and labor  compliance.  The  inspector  and the alternate  inspector  have  over  30
  years  of experience  in the industry,  which  provides  the ability  to ensure  the Project  is
  constructed  in accordance  with  the plans and specifications.

  *  Similar  Projects  - NV5's  core specialties  are construction  management  and inspection
  of Public  Works  projects.  NV5  completed  numerous  projects  of similar  scope.

The  scope  of  services  in  the  proposed  Agreement  consists  of  construction  management,
construction  inspection,  and labor  compliance.

  ANALYSIS:  The South Gate Park Weils  Reservoir  Intercomectton  Project  is included  in the
  Fiscal  Year  2025/26  Capital  Improvement  Program  as part  of the PFAS  Removal  Treatment
  System  Project  and  is  funded  with  $7,409,974  in  Water  Funds.  As  the  first  phase  of

  1

  354
 construction,  the  Interconnection  Project  is intended  to improve  operational  reliability  and
system resiliei'icy  by allowing  the City  to directly  supply  potable  water  from  the distribution
system to the South Gate Park Reservoir  during periods when groundwater  production  at the site
is  reduced  or  internipted.  This added redundancy  is particularly  important  as the City continues
addressing  PFAS-related  impacts  on groundwater  wells  and maintaining  compliance  with
evolving  water quality  regulations.

Staff completed  a formal  public  bidding  process for the project  and determined  that JA Salazar
submitted  the  lowest  responsive  and responsible  bid.  Staff  reviewed  the  contractor's  bid
proposal,  licensing,  references,  and qualifications  and determined  the contractor  possesses the
necessary experience  and capability  to successfully  complete  the work.  Approval  of the contract
will  allow  the  City  to proceed  with  this  critical  infrastructure  improvement  and continue
strengthening  the reliability  of the City's  water system.

BACKGROUND:  The  City's  water  system  consists  of more  than  135  miles  of  water
pipelines,  eight  active  groundwater  wells,  and multiple  water production  facilities.  One of the
City's  primary  water  production  sites  is  located  at South  Gate  Park  and  includes  four
groundwater  wells,  a water reservoir,  and an on-site  treatment  system. Currently,  groundwater
produced  by two of the wells has been impacted  by PFAS contamination.  If additional  wells  at
the site are impacted  and required  to be taken offline,  it is critical  that the reservoir  remain
operational  to m,aintain  reliable  water service,  adequate system pressure,  and fire protection  for
the community

To address this need, staff is proposing  the South Gate Park Reservoir  Interconnection  Project,
which  is budgeted  in the Fiscal  Year 2025/26  Capital  Improvement  Program.  The project  will
construct  a water mainline  connection  between  the reservoir  and the City's  water  distribution
system, allowing the City to directly supply potable water to the reservoir independent of certain
well  operations.  The project  will  also improve  operational  reliability  by allowing  the City  to
continue  delivering  water  from  the South  Gate Park reservoir  when  groundwater  wells  are
temporarily  unavailable  due to maintenance,  equipment  failure,  or regulatory  requirements.

Staff solicited  bids for the construction  of this improvement  on March 12, 2026, and received  ten
(10) bids on April  16, 2026. Following  review  of the submitted  bids, staff recommend  awarding
the construction  contract  to JA Salazar as the lowest responsive  and responsible  bidder.

  SUBJECT:  NOTICE OF COAIPLETI()N  FOR THE AUTOMATIC  II%'IETH,RREADING
  UPGRADE,  PHASE IV, CITY PROJECT  N0. 685-WTR

  PURPOSE:  Construction of the Project is completed and the retention payment to the
  contractor is due, Section 7107 of the Public Contract Code requires the City to accept
  completion of the Project and issue public notice of such, prior to releasing the retention
  payment.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS: The City Council will corisider:
  a, Approving Deductive Change Order No, I to Contract No. 2025-02-CC with JA Salazar
  Construction & Supply Corporation for the Autonnatic Meter Reading ("AMR") Upgrade,
  Phase IV, City Project No. 685-WTR, reducing the contract amount by $112,145;
  b, Authorizing the City Manager to execute Deductive Change Order No. 1 to Contract No.
  2025-02-CC;
  c, Accepting completion of the Automatic Meter Reading ("AMR") Upgrade, Phase IV,
  City Project No. 685-WTR by JA Salazar Consttuction & Supply Corporation, effective
  October 31, 2025; and
  d. Directing  the City Clerk to file a Notice  of Completion  with  Los Angeles County
  Registrar  Recorder'sOffice,

  FISCAL IMPACT:  There is no impact to the General Fund, Deductive Change Order No. 1 to
  Contract No, 2025-02-CC decreases the overall construction cost by $112,145.  The final
  construction contract amount was'$l,496,409, and it was fully funded with Water Funds.

  ANALYSIS:  Construction of the Automatic Meter Reading ("AMR")  Upgrade, Phase IV
  Project is complete. The project replaced aging water meters witl'i AMR ineters within Meter
  Route Cycle 3 located on the west side of the City. During cotstruction, staff deteri'nined that
  certain meters, transmitters, and meter boxes identified in the original bid schedule did not
  require replacement or installation. As a result, the final quantities installed were less than
  originally anticipated, resulting in a reduction to the final contract amount reflected in Chaxige,
  Order No. 1.

  1

  404
 Construction and installation  activities were completed in October 2025, and all remaining
unused materials were delivered in April 2026, allowing staff to finalize quantities and reconcile
the contract amount. With the work now complete, staff are preparing to release the final
retention payment to JA Salazar Construction & Supply Corporation.  Pursuant to tlie California
Public Contract Code, the City must first file a Notice of Completion, which formally notifies
concerned parties that the project has been completed and initiates tlie required 35-day lien
period. If no liens or claims are filed during that period, the City will release the retention
payment and any remaining  amount due under the contract.

BACKGROUND:  The City's water system is equipped with more than 14,000 water meters, of
which over 5,885 have been converted to AMR technology as part of the City's ongoing  water
infrastructure modernization efforts. The AMR Upgrade, Phase IV Project signifies completion
of another major phase of the City's AMR conversion program and included the replacement of
more than 1,700 aging water meters within Meter Route Cycle 3 on the west side of the City.
The upgraded AMR system improves meter reading efficiency, enhances water usage monitoring
capabilities, reduces manual labor requirements, and supports more accurate and timely water
billing services for residents and businesses.

On January 14, 2025, the City Council approved an Agreement with JA Salazar Construction &
Supply Corporation for the construction of the AMR Upgrade, Phase IV, City Project No. 685-
WTR, in the amount of $1,608,555. The project included the replacement of approximately
1,730 water meters with AMR meters to improve operational efficiency and modernize  the
City's  water  meter  reading  system.

JA Salazar Construction & Supply Corporation successfully completed the project in October
2025. Following completion of the work and reconciliation  of final installed quantities, staff
detennined that certain meters, transmitters, and meter boxes were not needed for installation.
Accordingly,  Deductive Change Order No. 1 to Contract No. 2025-02-CC reduces the contract
amount by $112,145 resulting in a revised contract amount of $1,496,409.

The City Council may now accept the Project as complete. The Notice of Completion  can now
be filed with the Los Angeles County Registrar Recorder's Office.

 ANALYSIS:  Pursuant  to  the  California  Public  Contract  Code,  the  City  must  comply  with
specific  requirements  before  issuing  final  payment  on a construction  contract.  In accordance  with
Section  7107  of the Public  Contract  Code,  the City  must  first  formally  accept  the completed
work  and issue a Notice  of Completion  before  releasing  the final  retention  payment.  The Notice
of  Completion  serves  as a formal  declaration  that  all  work  under  the  contract  has  been
completed.  It also initiates  the statutory  period  during  which  subcontractors,  suppliers,  and other
interested  parties  may  assert  any remaining  lien  claims  against  the project.  During  this period,
the City  retains  the right  to withhold  all or a portion  of the retention  payment  to satisfy  any valid
claims.  With  construction  now  complete,  staff  recommend  that the City  Council  approve  the
Notice  of Completion,  thereby  initiating  the process  to release  the final  payment  in accordance
with  applicable  law.

The budget  analysis  of final  project  expenditure  has been  completed,  and all costs  have  been
reconciled.  An  additional  appropriation  of  $250,000  is recommended  to  fund  outstanding
administrative  and  staffing  costs  associated  with  the  Project.  Staff  recommend  :tunding  this
appropriation  with  Measure  M  and Proposition  C fiinds,  allowing  these  transportation-related
expenditures  to be paid using  restricted  transportation  funding  sources.

BACKGROUND:  Construction  of  the  Tweedy  Mile  Complete  Streets  Project  has  been
completed.  The  Project  delivered  safety,  circulation,  landscaping,  and  beautification
improvements  along  Tweedy  Boulevard  between  Dearborn  Avenue  and  Dorothy  Avenue,
including  pavement  rehabilitation,  new  sidewalks  and ADA-compliant  curb  ramps,  enhanced
crosswalks  with  flashing  beacons,  traffic-calming  features,  upgraded  signage  and  transit
amenities,  new  landscaping,  bicycle  sharrows,  and bicycle  racks.  These  improvements  enhance
pedestrian  and vehicular  safety,  improve  access to public  transit  and bicycle  facilities,  address
deferred  infrastructure  maintenance,  and improve  the overall  quality  of life  along the corridor.

On July  9, 2024,  the City  Coiu'icil  awarded  Contract  No.  2024-56-CC  to Sequel  Contractors  Inc.
for construction  of the Project  in the amount  of $7,745,175.  A total  of 16 change  orders,  totaling

work  necessary  to complete  construction  and included  a $350,000  incentive  payment  authorized
by the City  Council  for completion  of the Project  on an expedited  construction  schedule.

Construction  of  the  Project  was  completed  on  July  9, 2024.  The  work  was  performed  in
accordance  with  the  approved  plans  and  specifications  and  was  completed  with  acceptable
quality  and workmanship,  within  the authorized  budget  and contract  schedule.  The contractor  has
satisfactorily  fulfilled  all contractual  obligations.

The City  Council  may now  accept  the Project  as complete.  The Notice  of Completion  can now
be filed  with  the Los Angeles  County  Registrar  Recorder's  Office.

SUBJECT:  AMENDMENT  N0. 2 TO CONTRACT N0. 2023-65-CC  WITH  PIPE TEC,
INC. TO FUND EMERGF,NCY  STORM DRAIN RF,PAIRS

PURPOSE: To approve Amendment No. 2 to Contract No. 2023-65-CC with Pipe Tec, Inc. to
fund emergency storm drain repair work that was performed in Hollydale Regional Park.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City Council will consider approving Amendment No. 2 to
the Agreement for Sanitary Sewer Main Closed-Circuit  Television Inspection Services
Agreement, Contract No, 2023-65-CC ("Agreement"), with Pipe Tec to fund emergency storm
drain repair work performed at Hollydale Regional Park.

FISCAL IMPACT:  Amendment No. 2 to the Agreement ("Amendment No. 2") is in the
amount of $34,000 and it will be funded with General Funds budgeted in the Fiscal Year
2025/26 Public Works Opetating Budget.

ANALYSIS:  In mid-April  2026, multiple sinkholes developed within the parking lot at
Hollydale Regional Park after an existing storm drainpipe failed undergtound, City staff
conducted an emergency investigation on April 20, 2026, which found that approximately 60
linear feet of the aging metal pipe had deteriorated and created additional underground voids that
were not visible fromthe surface.

To restore safe conditions witbin the parking lot, the City utilized Pipe Tec, Inc. to perform
emergency storm drain repairs. The work included removing the failed pipe, cleaning the
existing storm drain system, installing new high-density polyethylene (HDPE) pipe, backfilling
the excavated areas, and restoring the pavement surface.

During construction, additional damage and deterioration were discovered that exceeded the
original anticipated scope of work. As a result, Amendment No. 2 is required to authorize
payment for the completed emergency repair work.

Constnuction activities commenced on April 23, 2026, and were completed on April 24, 2026.
Approval of Amendment No. 2 will authorize payment for the emergency repair services
performed,

  1

  489
 BACKGROUND:  The  City  owns  and  operates  municipal  storm  drain  systems  located  within
public  rights-of-way  and  public  facilities,  including  public  parks.  The  City  is responsible  for
maintaining  this  infrastructure  to ensure  its  safe  and  reliable  operation.  Given  that  the  City  is
more  than  100  years  old,  aging  infrastructure  conditions  are not  uncommon.  The  storm  drain
failure  at Hollydale  Regional  Park  is indicative  of this  aging  infrastructure  and  highlights  the
need  for  continued  evaluation  of the  system  as part  of a -future  Capital  Improvement  Program
(CIP)  project.

The  City  utilizes  the  services  of  Pipe  Tec,  Inc.  under  an  as-needed  services  contract  for
specialized  underground  utility  and  pipeline  services.  Their  core  services  include,  but  are not
limited  to, closed-circuit  television  (CCTV)  inspections,  pipeline  cleaning,  storm  drain  and sewer
system  maintenance,  emergency  underground  utility  repairs,  and related  rehabilitation  services.

The  Agreement  with  Pipe  Tec,  Inc.  was  approved  by the City  Council  on May  23, 2023,  in the
amount  of  $347,000  for  sanitary  sewer  main  closed-circuit  television  (CCTV)  inspection
services.  On May  12, 2026,  the City  Council  approved  Amendment  No.  1, which  extended  the
contract  term  by 12 months  and increased  the  contract  amount  by  $147,000,  bringing  the total
contract  amount  to $494,000.

Amendment  No.  2 will  increase  the contract  amount  by an additional  $34,000,  for a new  not-to-
exceed  contract  amount  of $528,000.

  PURPOSE:  To reallocate funds from the South Gate Police Department,  Heating,  Ventilat'on
  and Airconditioning  (SGPD-HVAC)  Replacement  Project  to  the  South  Gate  Emergency
  Operations Center (EOC) Project.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City Council will consider:
  a.  De-obligating $308,667 in Building Infrastnicture  and Maintenance  Funds from the EOC
  Renovation Project, City Project 582-ARC.
  b,  Reallocating  $308,667 in Building  Infrastucture  and Maintenance  Funds from the
  SGPD-HVAC  Renovation Project, City Project 667-GEN, to the South Gate Emergency
  Operations  Center, City Project No. 582-ARC,  to fully fiind construction  services.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  Thete is no impact  to the General  Fund, The proposed  reallocation  is
  $308,667 in Building Infrastructure and Maintenance Funds, The proposed budget for the EOC
  Project is $1,634,667, to be funded with $1,226,000 in Cal OES Grant Funds, $100,000 in
  AQMD Funds, and $308,667 in Building Infrastructure and Maintenance Funds.

  ANALYSIS:  The EOC Project received grant funding  from the U.S. Department  of Homeland
  Security/California Governor's Office of Emergency Services ("CAL OES") Grant Program, for
  the design and constnuction of a new Emergency Operations Center, The grant requires the City
  to proyide a Iocal match contribution. To satisfy this requirement, on October 14, 2025, the City
  Council  approved the appropriation  of $308,667  from the Building  Infrastructure and
  Maintenance (BIM) Fund to fund the required local match.

  However, that appropriation is no longer necessary, Staff have identified budget savings within
  the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Capital Improvement Program due to the South Gate Police Department
  HVAC Project being under budget. As a result, staff is recommending that $308,667 in available
  project savings be reallocated from the SGPD-HVAC  Project to the EOC Project to fund the
  required local match, allowing the previously  approved BIM Fund appropriation  to be de-
  obligated.

 BACKGROUND:  The South  Gate Emergency  Operational  Center  Project  was included  in the
Fiscal  Year 2024/25  Capital  Improvement  Program  ("CIP")  to relocate  the City's  existing  EOC
from  the basement  of the  South  Gate  Police  Department  to a new  facility  within  the  Civic
Center.  The project  proposes  repurposing  a portion  of the South  Gate Museum  into  a modern
Emergency  Operations  Center  capable  of supporting  emergency  coordination,  disaster  response,
and continuity  of government  operations  during  major  incidents  and emergencies.

The  proposed  facility  is  designed  to  serve  a dual  purpose.  Under  normal  operations,  the
improved  space  will  'function  as a community  room,  conference  room,  and  museum  area
accessible  to the public.  During  emergency  activations,  the facility  will  transition  into  a fully
operational  EOC.  As part of the project,  certain  museum  displays  within  the project  area will  be
relocated  or incorporated  into  the  redesigned  space  to preserve  the  museum  character  and
maintain  public  viewing  opportunities  to the extent  practical.

On February  25, 2025,  the City  Council  adopted  a Resolution  authorizing  the submission  of a
grant  application  to Cal OES to secure funding  for the design  and construction  of the new EOC
facility.  Cal  OES  subsequently  approved  the  application  and  awarded  $1,226,000 in grant
:tunding  for the project.  On October  14, 2025, the City  Council  approved  a funding  appropriation
to fund the local match  contribution.

On January  13,  2026,  the City  Council  awarded  a professional  services  agreement  to Black
O'Dowd  and Associates,  Inc.  dba BOA  Architecture  to prepare  the  design  and construction
documents  for the South  Gate Emergency  Operational  Center,  City  Project  No.  582-ARC.  The
design  of the project  is now underway  and anticipated  to be completed  in November  2026.

GOVERNOR5S OFFI(J  OF EMF,RGENCY  SERVICF,S ("CAL OE8") GRANT FUNDS
FOR THE EMERGNECY  OPERATION  CENTER ("EOC") PROJF,CT, CITY PROJECT
N0. 582-ARC

PURPOSE:  Approval of the Resolution will authorize the submittal of an application for
grant funding to the California Governor's Office Of Emergency Services ("Cal OES") for the
Emeqai70perationCenter("EOC")Project  ("Project").

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will consider:
  a. AdoptingaResolutionauthorizingtheapplicationfortheCaliforniaGovernor'sOffice
  Of Emergency Services, requesting $1,226,000 in grant funds, for the Emergency
  Operations Center, City Project No. 582-ARC; and
  b. Authorizing the City Manager, or his designee, to execute, on behalf of the City, all
  documents requiredto submit the application andimplement the grant.

FISCAL IMPACT:  There is no itnpact to the General Fund, The grant application requests
$1,226,000 to fund the Project, however, it also includes a $408,667 commitment in matching
funds for a total project budget of $1,634,667.  Staff is teviewing funding options for the
matching funds thus as of the date of this Council Meeting a funding source(s) has not been
selected.

ANALYSIS:  CalOEShasallocated$l,226,000ingrantfundstofundtheconstructionofanew
EOC within the City Hall grounds. To secure the Brarit funds, the Cal OES requires a Resolution
from the City Council authorizing the application and use of the funds. Key points of the
required Resolution include:

  *  The Resolution authorizes the submission of an application to apply for the Cal OES
  grant in the amourit of $1,226,000 and commits to a local match requirement of
  $408,667, for a total budget of $1,634,667.

  *  The City certifies that sufficient  funds will be available to complete and maintain the
  project.

  516
   *  The City Manager, or his designee, is authorized to  handle  ail project-related
  negotiations, including agreements and payment requests.

BACKGROUND:  The South Gate Police Station, built in 1948, houses an Emergency
Operations Center ("EOC") in a subterranean section of the building. This location is prone to
flooding, Lacks ADA-compliant  access, and faces significant counication  challenges due to
the thiclc concrete walls. Given that effective communication is critical for emergency response,
staff tecommends relocating the EOC to ensure reliable operations during major events,

The project relocates the existing EOC from the SGPD basement to a new facility at the Civic
Center by repurposing  a portion of the museum to meet modern EOC requirements, The section
of the museum is planned to serve a dual purpose: m as-needed EOC and a Community
room/Museum.  Daily, the improved section will serve for conference room, community room
and a Museum. However, when the EOC is activated, that will be shut down to the public and
the EOC will be activated.

Some  of the displays in this portion of the museum  that will be improved will be relocated to the
easterly  side of the museum section, They will continue to be available for public viewing  to the
extent practical.  Other displays will be integrated into the room keeping part of the Museum
experience  while  still allotting appropriate space for the EOC needs.

As  a note, the originally  proposed relocation was to 8640 California Avenue (South Gate
Courthouse).  However,  that presented significant challenges, including asbestos removal,
seisrnic retrofitting  to comply with the 2024 Building Code, and insufficient staff parking. The
Civic Center location avoids these issues, making it a more suitable choice for the new EOC.

The proposed budget is $1,634,667. Work includes, but is not limited to, upgrading electrical and
mechanical  systems for proper heating and air conditioning, a backup generator, equipping the
space with televisions, tables, computers, desks, radios, and cell phones to support emergency
operations. The proposed budget will be expended as summarized below.

  SUBJH,CT:  AUTHORIZATION  TO INCREASE BLANI(ET  PURCHASF, ORDER FOR
  ASPHALT MATERIALS  PURCHASE,S

  PURPOSE: To increase the Blanket Purchase Order authority for agphalt materials to allow
  paytnent  of outstanding  invoices.

  RECOI!IMENDED  ACTION: The City Council will consider appro'ving a $10,805 increase to
  the Blanket Purchase Order for asphalt materials to cover current expenditures and outstanding
  invoices.

  FISCAL IMPACT: There is no impact to !he General Fund. The proposed inpease to the
  Blanket Purchase Order for asphalt materials is $10,805, and it is funded with Gas Tax and
  Water Funds budgeted in the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Public Works Operating Budget.

  ANALYSIS: The Public Works Department is responsible for maintaining the City's roadway
  pavement, which requires the year-round purchase of asphalt materials for routine maintenance
  activities such as pothole repairs and sl6n patching. The current Blanket Purchase Order (BPO)
  for asphalt materials has exhausted its authorized funding amount of $46,000 and currently
  reflects a negative balance of $301. In addition, outstanding invoices totaling $10,504 remain
  unpaid, resulting in a total funding shortfaU of $10,805.

  Accordingly, it is necessary to increase the BPO authority to a total amount of $56,805. Under
  the City's procurement guidelines, staff may administratively increase a BPO up to $49,999;
  however, the revised atnount exceeds that threshold and therefore requires City Council
  approval. Approval of this request will allow staff to process the outstanding invoices and
  continue essential street maintenance operations.

  The increase in expenditures beyond the annual $46,000 budget is primarily attributed to rising
  asphalt material costs. Asphalt is a petroleum-based product, and recent increases in oil prices
  have directly impacted asphalt pricing and overan street maintenance material costs.

  I

  520
 BACKGRO{JND:  The Public Works Department routinely utilizes Blanket Purchase Orders
(BPOs) to procure asphalt materials needed to support daily street maintenance operations
throughout the City. These materials are regularly used for pothole repairs, pavement restoration,
utility trench repairs, emergency roadway repairs, and other routine maintenance activities
necessary  to maintain safe and functional roadway conditions for the public.

Over the past year, expenditures under the current asphalt materials BPO increased at a faster
pace than originally  anticipated due to a combination of higher material usage demands and
escalating asphalt prices. Asphalt is a petroleum-based product, and fluctuations in oil prices
have significantly  increased the cost of asphalt materials and related roadway maintenance
supplies  citywide.

As a result, the current BPO exceeded its authorized funding limit. To prevent additional
overages, Public Works staff directed field crews to discontinue use of the existing BPO and
transition purchases to an alternate asphalt materials BPO with Blue Diamond. This temporary
measure has allowed the Department to maintain continuity  of critical street maintenance
operations while staff process the necessary purchasing adjustments.

Maintaining  adequate funding authority for asphalt material purchases is essential to ensure the
uninternupted delivery of roadway maintenance services, timely repair of deteriorated pavement
conditions, and continued protection of public safety. Approval of the requested increase will
allow the City to process outstanding vendor invoices, restore sufficient purchasing authority,
and continue routine street maintenance operations in compliance with City procurement
requirements.

  SUBJECT:  CITY  COUNCIL  APPOINTMENTS  TO  THE  VARIOUS  CITY
  COMMISSIONS,  COMMITTEES  AND  BOARDS

  PURPOSE:  Under  the South  Gate Municipal  Code,  City  Council  Members  are authorized  to
  nominate  individuals  to serve on various  City  Commissions,  Committees,  and Boards,  subject  to
  ratification  by the City  Council.  This  item  was placed  on tlie agenda  at the request  of Council
  Member  Maria  del Pilar Avalos  to remove  an existing  appointment.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The  City  Council  will  consider  ratifying  the motion  made  by
  Council  Member  Maria  del Pilar  Avalos  to remove  Eric  Trujillo  as her representative  from  the
  Parks & Recreation  Commission.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  None.

  ANALYSIS:  The removal  of the Commissioner  from  the Parks & Recreation  Cominission  must
  be ratified  by a majority  vote of the City  Council  and would  be effective  June 10, 2026.

  BACKGROUND:  According  to  South  Gate  Municipal  Code,  Title  1 Administration,  of
  Cl'iapter  1.09  Parks  and Recreation  Coinmission,  Section  1.09.060  Removal  from  office.  "Any
  coinrnissioner  may be removed  at any time  by a four-fifths  vote of the entire  city  council.  In the
  event a city  council  member  files  a written  request  with  the city manager  for the removal  of the
  commissioner  he/she  appointed  to  serve  on  the  parks  and recreation  commission,  then  the
  necessary  vote to effectuate  such removal  shall be a three-fifths  vote; however,  one of the voting
  city council  members  must be the city  council  member  who appointed  the commissioner  to serve
  on the parks and recreation  commission."
